headline: Lower egg costs and buybacks lift profit despite more debt
summary_short: Post Holdings' fiscal Q2 2026 (three months ended March 31, 2026) net sales rose 4.7% y/y to $2,042.9 million and operating profit grew 16.3% y/y to $211.9 million, with net earnings up 30.8% to $81.9 million ($1.56 diluted EPS) as lower egg costs lifted Foodservice profit and buybacks cut diluted shares 14.3% y/y.
summary_long: Operating profit rose 16.3% y/y on higher Foodservice profit (+79%, lower egg costs), plus gains in Refrigerated Retail and Weetabix, partly offset by weaker Post Consumer Brands profit (8th Avenue integration costs) and a $28.3 million Crystal Farms held-for-sale writedown in corporate expense. Net earnings grew 30.8% to $81.9 million despite $18.7 million higher interest expense from new 6.50%/6.25% notes issued to refinance debt and fund buybacks; diluted EPS rose 51.5% as shares fell 14.3% y/y on $716.5 million of six-month repurchases. Post affirmed FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance of $1,550-$1,580 million and capex guidance of $350-$390 million. Cash fell to $269.4 million; long-term debt rose to $7,629.1 million.
